findings.claim: Credited perfumers: Olivier Creed and Erwin Creed (sixth generation of the Creed family).
Production: Millésimé technique — hand-mixed, macerated and matured in Ury, France, unfiltered.

Community documentation records significant olfactive variation across production batches. Pre-2016 batches (notably 11Z01, 13ZZ01) are widely characterised as smokier birch, richer pineapple, stronger longevity — widely considered the reference standard by fragrance enthusiasts. 2022–2024 batches are consistently described as softer, sweeter, and less smoky. The 2025 presentation is described as 'more streamlined'. Creed has not publicly confirmed a reformulation. IFRA regulatory requirements and commercial scale are cited in community discussions as contributing factors to the character shift across batches.
findings.provenance: WebSearch — SEARCH_SNIPPET_ONLY, multiple community sources: Basenotes forum, Fragrantica community, heartnotes.co.uk, scentfile.com, parfumei.com.
findings.note: Batch variation is well-documented community discourse. It is relevant context for interpreting any Aventus note listing, as different batches present different olfactive expressions.

contradictions.description: Two substantially different note pyramids obtained. Current official creedboutique.com (DIRECT_ACCESS_SUCCESS, 2026) presents a simplified three-group pyramid with Pineapple Accord in the heart, no Oak Moss, no Ambergris, no Vanilla in base, no Apple in top. Historical Fragrantica-style listing (SEARCH_SNIPPET_ONLY, secondary) places Pineapple in the top, includes Oak Moss, Ambergris, Vanilla in base, and Apple in top. The discrepancy is consistent with documented batch variation and IFRA-driven ingredient changes. Both note presentations are recorded with their sources and access methods.
contradictions.resolution: BOTH_RECORDED — the creedboutique.com listing (current official, DIRECT_ACCESS_SUCCESS) is the authoritative current presentation; the historical listing is retained as contextual evidence of documented batch variation.

canonicalSummary: Aventus by Creed is a 2010 men's Eau de Parfum created by Olivier Creed and Erwin Creed using the Millésimé technique. The current official note presentation (creedboutique.com, 2026) lists Calabrian Bergamot, Sicilian Lemon & Blackcurrant Leaf Accord (top); Pineapple Accord, Pink Pepper & Jasmine Accord (heart); Birch, Patchouli & Musk Accord (base). Historical note listings include additional materials (Apple, Oak Moss, Ambergris, Vanilla) consistent with the well-documented batch variation discourse. Creed has not publicly confirmed reformulation. All findings in this dossier concern the reference fragrance only and do not constitute evidence about Maison Skye & Rose's inspired formulation.
